Target files: packages/miniflare/src/index.ts, packages/miniflare/test/dev-registry.spec.ts, .changeset/dev-registry-crash-restart-bindings.md. Title: [miniflare] Keep cross-process bindings working after a workerd crash restart (Ref: https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/16327)

workarounds.symptom: [vitest-plugin] cloudflare.config.ts Durable Object binding to the Worker's own class fails: "no such service is defined"
workarounds.workaround: Fix: [config] Fix Durable Object self-references without changing deployment targets. Target files: packages/deploy-helpers/src/deploy/helpers/durable-object-container-applications.ts, packages/deploy-helpers/src/preview/preview.ts, packages/deploy-helpers/src/preview/shared.ts. Durable Object bindings that explicitly name the Worker itself failed to start in the Vitest plugin and were rejected when attaching a container. Recognize those self-references where the effective Worker identity is known, while preserving explic... (Ref: https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/16013)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: [Bug]: bare `@torch.compile` in `kimi_k25_vit` compiles outside the compilation lifecycle and pins `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` process-wide
workarounds.workaround: Fix: [Bugfix] Avoid eager torch.compile in Kimi K2.5 vision helper. Target files: vllm/model_executor/models/kimi_k25_vit.py. `get_rope_shape` in the Kimi K2.5 vision encoder was decorated with bare `torch.compile`, and an eager wrapper invoked it on the first input key. This could initialize Triton before vLLM's compilation lifecycle configured its cache directories, causing warm-cache reload failures. (Ref: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53011)

workarounds.symptom: Deep-copying a self-referential model changes its object graph
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Fix deep copy of self-referential models. Target files: pydantic/main.py, pydantic/root_model.py, tests/test_construction.py. Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/14093. (Ref: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/14116)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: Humming FP8 linear crashes on per-tensor/per-channel FP8 weights, so FP8 models cannot start with VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 on Ampere
workarounds.workaround: Fix: [Bugfix][Quantization] Fix Humming FP8 linear for per-tensor/per-channel FP8 weights. Target files: vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py, vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/fp8.py, vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online/fp8.py. . With the Humming FP8 linear kernel, `fp8` checkpoints with per-tensor weight scales and online `fp8_per_tensor` / `fp8_per_channel` quantization crash while loading weights. On Ampere with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, Humming is the only FP8 linear kernel left (Marlin opts out... (Ref: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60163)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: Rust vllm-bench accepts --max-concurrency 0 and hangs forever (Python rejects it since #54887)
workarounds.workaround: Fix: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Rust vllm-bench accepts --max-concurrency 0 and hangs forever (Python rejects it since #54887). Target files: rust/src/bench/src/config.rs, rust/src/bench/src/mm_processor.rs, rust/src/bench/src/sweep.rs. Rust `vllm-bench` accepted `--max-concurrency 0` and then hung forever on `Semaphore::new(0)`, while Python `vllm bench serve` rejects 0 since #54887. This change rejects 0 fail-fast on every Rust bench path that builds a concurrency semaphore: (Ref: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64390)

workarounds.symptom: websearch_interception chat-completions agentic follow-up misroutes model: 'LLM Provider NOT provided ... model=mantle/...'
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(websearch)!: keep the provider prefix on the agentic follow-up model. Target files: litellm/integrations/websearch_interception/handler.py, litellm/litellm_core_utils/chat_completion_agentic_loop.py, litellm/litellm_core_utils/core_helpers.py. Web search follow-ups now keep the caller's full model, so Bedrock Mantle and OpenRouter org models stop failing or reaching the wrong provider (Ref: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/38885)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug] Multiple system messages sent to non-OpenAI providers when using Responses API with developer role messages
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(llms): move later developer messages for models declared system-first. Target files: litellm/constants.py, litellm/llms/anthropic/chat/transformation.py, litellm/llms/anthropic/messages/native/transformation.py. Codex and other Responses API clients send a developer item after the first input item. LiteLLM turns it into a `system` message in place, and system-first chat templates such as Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.8 answer 400 `System message must be at the beginning` (Ref: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/48897)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: Gemini context caching with custom api_base uses invalid cache URL and auth header
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(vertex_ai): build the cachedContents collection URL under a custom api_base. Target files: litellm/llms/vertex_ai/context_caching/vertex_ai_context_caching.py, litellm/llms/vertex_ai/vertex_llm_base.py, litellm/types/llms/vertex_ai.py. Gemini and Vertex AI context caching failed behind a custom `api_base`, because Google rejects the `models/<model>:cachedContents` URL the proxy built (Ref: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/44783)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: Editing a reusable credential can overwrite real secrets with masked placeholders
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(credentials): keep the stored secret when PATCH echoes its masked read-back. Target files: litellm/litellm_core_utils/litellm_logging.py, litellm/proxy/credential_endpoints/endpoints.py, tests/unit/proxy/credential_endpoints/test_endpoints.py. Reading a credential back from the API gives you its secrets masked, like `sk****EA`. Sending that object back with PATCH to edit another field saved the mask as the key, breaking every model on it. The Admin UI's Edit Credential dialog did the same to Vertex credentials (Ref: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/48950)

workarounds.symptom: Bedrock audio transcription hardcodes a system message in the Rust codec, breaking Voxtral (400 'Found system messages at indexes [0] and audio chunks')
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(bedrock): omit system prompt from audio transcription and report its token usage. Target files: litellm-rust/crates/llms-types/src/formats/audio_transcription/response.rs, litellm-rust/crates/llms/src/bedrock/audio_transcription/mod.rs, litellm/cost_calculator.py. Bedrock Voxtral transcription through `/v1/audio/transcriptions` always failed with a 400, because LiteLLM sent a system prompt that Voxtral on Bedrock refuses next to audio. This PR drops that prompt (Ref: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/41565)

workarounds.symptom: mcp-server-fetch: `fetch` prompt returns JSON-RPC error code 0 with the raw exception text for an invalid URL
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(fetch): reject an invalid prompt URL with -32602. Target files: src/fetch/src/mcp_server_fetch/server.py, src/fetch/tests/test_prompt_url.py, src/fetch/tests/test_protocol.py. The `fetch` prompt passed its `url` argument straight to httpx. A malformed URL such as `http://[::1` raises `httpx.InvalidURL`, which is not an `httpx.HTTPError`, so it escaped `fetch_url`'s handler and the prompt's `except ToolError`, and the SDK answered with its generic fallback for an unhandled exception. On current `v2/main` (aft... (Ref: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/pull/5358)

workarounds.symptom: ChatAnthropic/_create_usage_metadata crashes with TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +=: 'int' and 'NoneType' when cache_creation contains an explicit None value
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(anthropic): handle null cache-creation token counts. Target files: libs/partners/anthropic/langchain_anthropic/chat_models.py, libs/partners/anthropic/tests/unit_tests/test_chat_models.py. Prevent `ChatAnthropic` from crashing when a provider returns null cache-creation TTL counts. Preserve omission of null token details and correct the regression test to expect the missing key. (Ref: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/pull/41553)
